posts.title: HiddenLayer nabs $100M as enterprises rush to secure their AI deployments | TechCrunch
posts.author: Ram Iyer
posts.summary: AI security firm HiddenLayer announced a $100 million Series B round to accelerate its protection tools for generative AI models, agents, and toolchains. The company says its annual recurring revenue has surged into the tens of millions, fueled by new contracts with financial services, large tech firms, and U.S. defense agencies. It plans to broaden its product suite and expand into Europe as the market for AI safeguards expands rapidly.

posts.title: India's richest man now wants to turn aging computers into AI-ready PCs | TechCrunch
posts.author: Jagmeet Singh
posts.summary: Reliance Jio has opened its JioPC cloud‑PC service to any internet user in India, allowing older computers to run AI‑ready workloads without hardware upgrades. Subscriptions start at ₹1,000 for two months and provide up to 16 GB of RAM and 1 TB of storage streamed from Jio’s data centers.

posts.title: Wonderful more than doubles its valuation to $5B in under 6 months | TechCrunch
posts.author: Ram Iyer
posts.summary: Israeli-Dutch AI startup Wonderful secured $550 million in a Series C round, pushing its valuation to $5 billion, more than double its level six months ago. The funding, led by Insight Partners with participation from existing backers and new investor Salesforce, will accelerate product development and

posts.title: Larry Page's flying car company Pivotal loses its CEO | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sean O'Kane
posts.summary: Ken Karklin has left his role as CEO of Larry Page–backed Pivotal after more than four years, and board member Mike Ross has been appointed interim CEO. Pivotal, which began sales of its single-seat Helix two years ago (starting around $200,000), also operates the BlackFly platform that has logged over 10,000 flights and was used last month in an emergency response.
key_points: Ken Karklin departed as CEO after more than four years; Mike Ross named interim CEO.
Helix sales began two years ago with a starting price around $200,000; BlackFly has flown over 10,000 times and aided a response last month.

posts.title: Reliance's JioHotstar takes its streaming empire global — without sports | TechCrunch
posts.author: Ivan Mehta
posts.summary: Reliance Industries’ JioHotstar is expanding outside India for the first time, replacing Hotstar in the U.K., Canada, and Singapore on September 2 with apps on mobile and connected TVs. The service launches with more than 160,000 hours of Indian films, TV originals and live TV channels but will not offer live sports at debut due to existing content deals.
key_points: JioHotstar replaces Hotstar in the U.K., Canada, and Singapore on September 2
Launch includes 160,000+ hours of entertainment content but excludes live sports at debut

posts.title: Apple follows Google in adopting Trump’s ‘Lake America’ name | TechCrunch
posts.author: Kirsten Korosec
posts.summary: Apple updated Apple Maps to display Lake Ontario as "Lake America" for users in the United States, following Google and an executive order signed by President Trump on August 27. MapQuest refused to rename the lake and its iOS app climbed to No. 1 in U.S. App Store downloads as users sought alternatives.
key_points: Apple Maps shows "Lake America" to U.S. users after Trump’s August 27 executive order
MapQuest refused the rename and its iOS app reached No. 1 in U.S. App Store downloads

posts.title: AfterQuery reportedly becomes Y Combinator's fastest-ever unicorn, now valued at $3.2B | TechCrunch
posts.author: Julie Bort
posts.summary: AfterQuery, an AI training-data startup, raised a financing that values it at $3.2 billion — just five months after its April Series A of $30 million at a $300 million valuation, a more-than-10x increase. Y Combinator partner Gustaf Alströmer called it the accelerator’s fastest path to unicorn; the San Francisco company reported a $100 million annualized run rate in April, counts Nvidia, Legora and Motif Technologies as customers, and trains models by encoding professional practitioners’ decision-making.
key_points: Valued at $3.2 billion, up from a $300 million valuation after a $30M Series A in April
Reported $100 million annualized run rate in April; customers include Nvidia, Legora, Motif Technologies

posts.title: OpenAI's Astra model is on the way — and very good at breaking into computer systems | TechCrunch
posts.author: Tim Fernholz
posts.summary: OpenAI says its forthcoming Astra model meets its critical cybersecurity threshold and demonstrated offensive capabilities in internal tests, scoring perfectly on ExploitBench and reportedly discovering and exploiting two zero-day vulnerabilities. The company will preview Astra with selected testers, limit access to its most advanced cybersecurity features, and says it has added harness improvements, chain-of-thought monitoring, and risk-based response restrictions, though external evaluation details remain unclear.
key_points: OpenAI says Astra scored a perfect on ExploitBench and found and exploited two zero-day vulnerabilities
OpenAI will limit advanced access, preview with selected testers, and add safeguards including chain-of-thought monitoring and account risk restrictions

posts.title: Google's Android update tackles motion sickness, accessibility, and more | TechCrunch
posts.author: Lauren Forristal
posts.summary: Google announced five Android updates focused on accessibility, personalization, and item tracking, with several features using Gemini. Key additions include Motion Assist — a customizable bubble overlay to reduce motion sickness on Android 17 — and Guided Vision, which pairs the camera with Gemini to help blind and low-vision users on phones running Android 9 and newer.
key_points: Motion Assist: bubble overlay to reduce motion sickness — available on Android 17
Guided Vision: camera plus Gemini assists blind and low-vision users — Android 9 and newer

posts.title: X says attackers are targeting user accounts after the launch of X Money | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sarah Perez
posts.summary: Following the launch of X Money, attackers have been mass-triggering password reset requests against X accounts, prompting many unsolicited reset emails reported by users. X product engineer Mridul Singhai said the company is investigating and has found no evidence of successful breaches so far, while general counsel James Burnham warned of legal action and users were urged to enable two-factor authentication.
key_points: Mass password-reset requests targeted X users after X Money launched
X says investigation shows no evidence of breaches so far and advises enabling two-factor authentication

posts.title: John Ternus hypes 'huge launch next week' in first memo as Apple CEO | TechCrunch
posts.author: Amanda Silberling
posts.summary: John Ternus has taken over as Apple CEO, succeeding Tim Cook who led the company for 15 years. In his first memo he signaled a major launch next week ahead of Apple’s September 9 iPhone event, which is widely expected to unveil a foldable iPhone and a broader rollout of upgraded Siri AI.
key_points: John Ternus named Apple CEO, succeeding Tim Cook after 15 years
Apple’s September 9 iPhone event is expected to feature a foldable iPhone and expanded Siri AI rollout

posts.title: Anthropic's new Fable release is cheaper, less restrictive | TechCrunch
posts.author: Russell Brandom
posts.summary: Anthropic released Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1, twin versions of its latest AI model; Fable 5.1 is available on cloud platforms and via Anthropic’s API while Mythos 5.1 is limited to registered cybersecurity and life-sciences partners. The update reduces token costs and false-positive safeguards, introduces zero data retention with an Enterprise Frontier Safeguards option rolling out in the fall, and set new benchmark records including Terminal-Bench 4.0 and Humanity’s Last Exam.
key_points: Fable 5.1 is publicly available; Mythos 5.1 is restricted to registered cybersecurity and life-sciences partners.
Anthropic adds zero data retention and will offer Enterprise Frontier Safeguards in the fall, while stating it never trains on enterprise data without permission.

posts.title: Thrive's Kushner defends involvement in FIFA mess, hires Elon's go-to lawyer | TechCrunch
posts.author: Julie Bort
posts.summary: Thrive Capital founder Josh Kushner defended the firm’s involvement in a collapsed plan to create FIFA Forward Enterprise, saying the proposal sought to distribute World Cup commercial revenues more evenly but that Thrive would not have joined had it anticipated the political fallout. UEFA is pursuing legal action tied to Gianni Infantino and has sought court orders for Thrive to produce valuation models and deal documents; Thrive has hired Quinn Emanuel partner Alex Spiro to represent it.
key_points: Thrive agreed to lead a potential $4.2 billion secondary share purchase representing 20% of FIFA Forward Enterprise at a $20 billion valuation
Thrive retained Alex Spiro of Quinn Emanuel amid UEFA’s bid to compel documents in its case involving Gianni Infantino

posts.title: Who is John Ternus, the new Apple CEO? | TechCrunch
posts.author: Amanda Silberling
posts.summary: In April 2026 Tim Cook handed the Apple CEO role to John Ternus, the company’s senior vice president of hardware engineering, while Cook remains executive chairman. Ternus, 51, has worked at Apple for 25 years and will lead the company as it rolls out new hardware and expands its AI efforts, including a Siri upgrade powered by Google’s Gemini.
key_points: Ternus is 51 and has worked at Apple for 25 years.
He led Apple’s hardware engineering and oversaw products like AirPods, Apple Watch, Vision Pro and the MacBook Neo.

posts.title: Google's answer to Canva is an AI tool where you prompt instead of design | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sarah Perez
posts.summary: Google is launching Google Pics, a prompt-driven image creation and editing tool powered by its Nano Banana image-generation model, which will roll out to most Workspace customers and Google AI Pro or Ultra subscribers over the coming weeks. Integrated into Workspace starting with Docs and Slides (rolling out today) and later Drive, Google Pics offers object isolation and transformation, text modification and translation inside images, collaborative editing, and multiple generated variants, positioning it as a prompt-first alternative to Canva and Adobe Express.
key_points: Powered by the Nano Banana model; rolling out to most Workspace customers and Google AI Pro or Ultra subscribers over the coming weeks.
Built into Docs and Slides today with features for object isolation, image and text editing, collaborative workflows, and multiple generated variants.

posts.title: ChatGPT Health adds Epic integration for clinicians to import patient data | TechCrunch
posts.author: Ivan Mehta
posts.summary: OpenAI integrated ChatGPT Health with Epic’s EHR, enabling clinicians to import patient records from a system covering over 325 million patients and, in some deployments, access ChatGPT directly within EHR workflows for tasks like pre-visit review and clinical timelines. The integration is read-only, and OpenAI added a Healthcare Public Data plug-in that pulls from ClinicalTrials.gov, CMS Coverage, RxNorm, DailyMed and PubMed while allowing organizations with a Business Associate Agreement to use ChatGPT Work and related tools for compliant workflows.
key_points: ChatGPT Health integrates with Epic EHR to import patient data from a system covering over 325 million patients
Integration is read-only and includes a Healthcare Public Data plug-in sourcing ClinicalTrials.gov, CMS, RxNorm, DailyMed and PubMed

posts.title: Waymo goes on offense ahead of Tesla's Cybercab launch | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sean O'Kane
posts.summary: Waymo publicly criticized camera‑only, end‑to‑end neural approaches this week, citing more than 200 million real‑world miles and arguing that combining cameras, lidar, and radar is necessary for safe, fully autonomous operations. The timing coincides with Tesla preparing to unveil its two‑seat Cybercab on September 3, while Waymo expands into three new U.S. markets and operates about 4,000 robotaxis across 14 cities serving roughly 500,000 paid trips per week.
key_points: Waymo cites 200+ million real‑world miles to support a multi‑sensor approach (camera, lidar, radar).
Tesla will unveil the two‑seat Cybercab on September 3 and has filings to produce over 125,000 annually.

posts.title: Sequoia-incubated Empirik launches with $21M to predict outages before they happen | TechCrunch
posts.author: Marina Temkin
posts.summary: Empirik, incubated by Sequoia, has spun out and raised $21 million in seed funding from Sequoia, Canapi, and Alumni Ventures and named Kartik Chandrayana as CEO. The company uses AI to track system changes across large infrastructures, flag risky updates, and predict outages to help SRE and DevOps teams automate incident prevention; early customers include S&P Global and Guardant Health.
key_points: Raised $21M seed from Sequoia, Canapi, and Alumni Ventures
AI observability platform predicts outages by tracking changes and flagging risky updates

posts.title: GoPro to be acquired for $285M, will remain a public company | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sean O'Kane
posts.summary: GoPro will be acquired in a merger with Starman Optical for $285 million; Starman will pay $1.14 per share, leave GoPro shareholders with about 10% of the combined company, and wipe GoPro’s $92 million debt with the deal expected to close by year-end. Starman, part of Starman Holding (owner of Incase, Incipio and Griffin), was incorporated in Delaware on August 31 and via its Starman New Photonics unit (created in 2025) plans to onshore manufacturing and expand GoPro into consumer, commercial and defense imaging markets.
key_points: Acquisition: $285 million; $1.14 per share, shareholders to retain ~10% of combined company
Deal will eliminate GoPro’s $92 million debt and is expected to close by the end of the year

posts.title: Amazon Alexa can now alert you when something new might tempt you to shop | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sarah Perez
posts.summary: Amazon on Tuesday added a feature called 'Update Me When' to Alexa for Shopping that sends personalized notifications when new products, releases, or events might prompt a purchase. The company also emphasized other Alexa shopping AI tools such as price tracking with discount alerts and an option to automatically buy items when conditions are met.
key_points: 'Update Me When' sends personalized notifications for new products, releases, or events.
Alexa can track prices, send discount alerts, and optionally auto-purchase items.

posts.title: AIR raises $50M to help companies vet the skills and add-ons AI agents use | TechCrunch
posts.author: Ram Iyer
posts.summary: AI security startup AIR, founded by Yair Saban and Niv Hoffman, came out of stealth after raising $50 million in two seed rounds ($10M led by Sequoia and $40M led by Greenoaks) to monitor the emerging software supply chain for AI agents. Its platform discovers agents across enterprise environments, continuously vets and enforces whitelists for skills and add-ons (filtering about 27% of add-ons), and serves more than 20 customers with particular traction in financial services and pharmaceuticals.
key_points: Raised $50M across two seed rounds ($10M and $40M) led by Sequoia and Greenoaks
Platform discovers agents, vets skills/add‑ons, enforces whitelists and filters ~27% of add-ons found

posts.title: Microsoft 365 outage drags on, but things are improving | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sarah Perez
posts.summary: Microsoft is on day two of a multi-day outage that has disrupted Outlook email and several Microsoft 365 services after an Exchange Online authentication misconfiguration. The company says mitigations have gradually restored mail flow and search for many users, but services are not yet fully recovered and it has entered extended monitoring.
key_points: Exchange Online authentication misconfiguration affected Outlook, SharePoint, Teams and other Microsoft 365 services
Microsoft reports gradual recovery after mitigations and is in an extended monitoring phase

posts.title: Fambot introduces an 'AI chief of staff' for families | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sarah Perez
posts.summary: Fambot, founded by Greg Karlin, David Reich and Jason Morrow, is offering an “AI chief of staff” for families that connects email, calendar and WhatsApp to produce daily checklists and proactively surface upcoming family logistics. The startup tested with over 1,000 families, raised $3.5 million in pre-seed funding led by NextView Ventures and Baukunst, and is in free beta on iOS, Android and the web while using models that do not train on user data.
key_points: integrates email, calendar and WhatsApp to create daily family to-dos
$3.5M pre-seed raised; tested by 1,000+ families and free in beta

posts.title: Florida and Texas move to block Flock cameras over privacy concerns | TechCrunch
posts.author: Zack Whittaker
posts.summary: Florida and Texas are moving to end their relationships with surveillance company Flock amid reports of misuse, data privacy concerns and accuracy problems. Florida’s Department of Transportation ordered license-plate readers removed statewide within 30 days, and Texas directed agencies to stop funding Flock after abuses including an indictment of a Lufkin officer on 100 felony counts; Flock operates about 130,000 readers in the U.S.
key_points: Florida DOT ordered statewide removal of Flock license-plate readers within 30 days
Texas halted state funding for Flock following reports of abuse and a Lufkin officer indictment

posts.title: This startup is fuel-injecting hydrogen to make cargo ships more efficient | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sean O'Kane
posts.summary: Newlight, a San Francisco Bay Area startup co-founded by Evyatar Cohen and Haran Cohen Hillel, has developed a retrofit hydrogen-injection system that monitors engine conditions to inject compressed hydrogen and reduce diesel consumption and emissions. On an 8,500-nautical-mile commercial voyage aboard a 650-foot Lomar Shipping bulk carrier the system cut fuel use by 24% and CO2 emissions by 28%; the company raised $9 million in seed funding and has agreements to install the tech on 12 vessels.
key_points: Reduced fuel consumption 24% and CO2 emissions 28% on an 8,500-nautical-mile Singapore–Ghana voyage on a 650-foot Lomar Shipping bulk carrier
Raised $9 million seed round and signed agreements to install the system on 12 vessels

posts.title: Waymo accelerates robotaxi expansion with launches in Denver, San Diego, and Tampa | TechCrunch
posts.author: Kirsten Korosec
posts.summary: Waymo has opened public robotaxi service in Denver, San Diego, and Tampa, expanding its commercial operations to 14 U.S. cities and inviting riders on a rolling basis as it scales. The company’s fleet tops 4,000 vehicles and includes Jaguar I‑Pace models plus about 300 Zeekr-made Ojai minivans, which are the only autonomous vehicles available to riders in Denver and San Diego.
key_points: Public robotaxi service launched in Denver, San Diego, and Tampa, bringing Waymo to 14 U.S. cities.
Fleet exceeds 4,000 vehicles; Ojai minivan (~300 units) is the sole autonomous model in Denver and San Diego.

posts.title: Help build the future of startups: Volunteer at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 | TechCrunch
posts.author: TechCrunch Events
posts.summary: TechCrunch is seeking volunteers for Disrupt 2026 at Moscone West, a three-day startup conference running October 13–15. Volunteers support the event operations, receive free three-day admission, and must apply by September 25.
key_points: Free admission for all three days (October 13–15)
Application deadline: September 25

posts.title: India's Unacademy sells to rival upGrad for $206M, about 94% less than its peak valuation | TechCrunch
posts.author: Jagmeet Singh
posts.summary: Unacademy has been acquired by rival upGrad in an all-stock deal that values the Bengaluru-based edtech group at ₹19.55 billion (about $206 million), roughly 94% below its $3.44 billion 2021 peak valuation. The transaction covers the entire group including PrepLadder, Graphy and Airlearn, leaves Gaurav Munjal as CEO, transfers shareholders to upGrad stock, and reportedly involves no planned layoffs while the company held about ₹9 billion in cash and roughly ₹4 billion in annual revenue.
key_points: Deal values Unacademy at ₹19.55 billion (~$206M), about 94% below its $3.44B 2021 peak
All-stock transaction: shareholders receive upGrad shares, Munjal stays as CEO, no layoffs planned

posts.title: If space data centers feel far-fetched, why not interstellar travel? | TechCrunch
posts.author: Tim Fernholz
posts.summary: A new non-profit called Fermi Explorer, started by Starcloud founders Philip Johnston, Adi Oltean and Ezra Feilden with program manager Garret Jameson, plans to send a small 1 kg, 10 cm-square probe toward Alpha Centauri using proven space technologies. The group says the ~$15 million mission would launch in 2029 on a rideshare, use low-power electric propulsion with about 12 years of activity before an 80,000-year coast, aiming to test the Fermi paradox rather than achieve interstellar flight within a human lifetime.
key_points: 1 kg, 10 cm-square probe targeted to Alpha Centauri
Planned $15 million launch in 2029 with an 80,000-year voyage

posts.title: Magna increases bet on battery swapping in India with $35M for Yuma | TechCrunch
posts.author: Jagmeet Singh
posts.summary: Magna International is investing an additional $35 million in Bengaluru-based Yuma Energy, increasing its stake above the 51% it took when the joint venture formed with Yulu. Yuma — which has completed more than 60 million swaps, deploys about 100,000 batteries across 400+ stations, and posted roughly ₹1 billion (~$10.5M) revenue for the year ending March 2026 — will use the funds to expand swapping infrastructure and double its battery fleet to serve high-mileage gig-economy riders across 18 Indian cities.
key_points: Magna invested $35 million to raise its stake in Yuma Energy
Yuma has 60M+ swaps, ~100,000 batteries, 400+ stations and ~₹1 billion revenue (FY March 2026)

posts.title: Lachy Groom backs Indian startup aiming to keep aircraft aloft for a year | TechCrunch
posts.author: Jagmeet Singh
posts.summary: Bengaluru startup Alteon, founded by 20-year-old Samay Sanghvi, raised $2.5 million in a pre-seed round led by Lachy Groom to develop small autonomous fixed-wing aircraft that aim to stay aloft for more than a year by harvesting energy from ocean winds via dynamic soaring. The company completed autonomous tests over the Bay of Bengal — seven O-shaped cycles at over 62 mph within 1 meter of the water — but has not yet demonstrated energy-neutral dynamic soaring and faces real-world low-altitude challenges.
key_points: $2.5M pre-seed led by Lachy Groom
Autonomous test: seven O-shaped cycles at >62 mph within 1 m of water

posts.title: Apple shares 'shocking evidence' against former employee accused of stealing company data for OpenAI | TechCrunch
posts.author: Amanda Silberling
posts.summary: Apple alleges in a lawsuit that former employee Chang Liu stole trade secrets, used a confidential Apple circuit schematic and a tool named after an internal engineering app while at OpenAI, and enlisted colleague Yu-Ting Peng to help destroy evidence. Liu’s old MacBook was handed over for investigation earlier this month, and Apple is seeking a preliminary injunction and expedited discovery as its initial filing says more than 400 former Apple employees now work at OpenAI.
key_points: Apple alleges Chang Liu used a confidential Apple circuit schematic and an internal-named tool at OpenAI
Apple seeks a preliminary injunction and expedited discovery; initial filing says more than 400 former Apple employees now work at OpenAI

posts.title: Polymarket reportedly raises $300 million from Donald Trump Jr.'s investment fund | TechCrunch
posts.author: Lucas Ropek
posts.summary: Polymarket has reportedly raised $300 million from 1789 Capital, the investment fund where Donald Trump Jr. is a partner, as part of a financing round sources say totals about $1 billion. The investment arrives while prediction markets face mounting legal challenges from states over sports wagers and federal regulators including the CFTC are contesting state authority.
key_points: 1789 Capital reportedly invested $300 million in Polymarket in a round said to be roughly $1 billion; the firm previously put $200 million into the site.
Prediction markets face legal pressure: at least 20 states are litigating over sports wagers and the CFTC has sued at least nine states.

posts.title: a16z brings growth fund to $8.5B days after launching new $1.1B fund | TechCrunch
posts.author: Julie Bort
posts.summary: Andreessen Horowitz expanded its fifth growth fund to $8.5 billion, adding $1.75 billion since it launched at $6.75 billion in January. Days earlier the firm also closed a $1.1 billion Machine Age Fund focused on AI hardware startups building chips, memory, networking and storage.
key_points: Growth fund increased to $8.5 billion, up $1.75 billion since January
Raised $1.1 billion Machine Age Fund targeting AI hardware startups

posts.title: A group funded by Andreessen, Horowitz, and Brockman plans data center ads to sway midterms | TechCrunch
posts.author: Julie Bort
posts.summary: Build American AI, tied to the Leading the Future (LTF) super PAC funded by Marc Andreessen, Ben Horowitz and OpenAI president Greg Brockman, plans multimillion-dollar ad campaigns promoting data centers in battleground states Kansas, Ohio and Wisconsin ahead of the midterms. OpenAI has publicly distanced itself from LTF, which launched with over $50 million, while Andreessen Horowitz–linked donors have disclosed more than $115 million in federal contributions this cycle.
key_points: Build American AI will run data-center advocacy ads in Kansas, Ohio, and Wisconsin with a multi-million dollar budget
Leading the Future (LTF) launched with over $50 million; Andreessen Horowitz–linked donors have disclosed over $115 million in federal contributions

posts.title: FTC accuses Amazon of running a ‘secret ad surcharge scheme’ in new lawsuit | TechCrunch
posts.author: Lauren Forristal
posts.summary: The FTC and 22 states sued Amazon, alleging that beginning in 2019 the company secretly added a “soft reserve price” and used a fake bidder to inflate prices in its Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands and Display ad auctions, effectively turning marketed second-price auctions into first-price outcomes. The complaint says the practice affected more than 1 million brands and sellers and may have generated tens of billions in extra revenue, while Amazon reported over $68 billion in advertising revenue last year and has disputed the allegations.
key_points: FTC and 22 states allege Amazon added a hidden “soft reserve” and fake bidder in ad auctions starting in 2019.
Allegedly affected more than 1 million brands and sellers; Amazon reported over $68 billion in ad revenue last year.

posts.title: The Pentagon now has its own version of ChatGPT and Grok | TechCrunch
posts.author: Kirsten Korosec
posts.summary: The Pentagon added ChatGPT Mil and Grok for Government to its secure GenAI.mil portal, providing tailored versions of OpenAI and SpaceX Starshield AI models to the Defense Department. The portal — launched last year — is designed to keep sensitive data out of consumer channels and has already onboarded more than 1.7 million of the department’s roughly 3 million civilian and military personnel.
key_points: ChatGPT Mil and Grok for Government were added to the GenAI.mil portal
GenAI.mil has onboarded over 1.7 million of the department’s roughly 3 million personnel

posts.title: Apply now to host a Side Event at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 | TechCrunch
posts.author: TechCrunch Events
posts.summary: TechCrunch is inviting applications for Side Events at its Disrupt 2026 conference in San Francisco, scheduled for October 13-15, with side events allowed from October 10-16

posts.title: Instagram puts new limits on undisclosed AI profiles | TechCrunch
posts.author: Lauren Forristal
posts.summary: Instagram announced it will rename its “AI creator” tag to “AI-generated profile” and will curb the reach of accounts that feature AI-generated personas without the label. The change aims to make AI disclosures clearer while exempting typical AI-assisted edits, and follows recent backlash over AI influencers and a Meta settlement.

posts.title: Apple's top App Store exec, Phil Schiller, follows wave of exits as CEO Tim Cook steps down | TechCrunch
posts.author: Lucas Ropek
posts.summary: Apple announced that longtime App Store leader Phil Sch

posts.title: Microsoft tests fix for latest hours-long Outlook outage | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sarah Perez
posts.summary: Microsoft confirmed a multi‑hour outage of its Exchange Online service on Monday, which disrupted Outlook email, calendar and authentication functions for many users. The company pinpointed a misconfigured authentication component, began testing a remediation on part of its infrastructure, and plans to roll out the fix more broadly once validated.
key_points: Microsoft traced the outage to a misconfigured authentication component in Exchange Online
A remediation is being tested on a portion of the infrastructure before a full rollout

posts.title: Kalshi bans George Santos for life over State of the Union bets | TechCrunch
posts.author: Kirsten Korosec
posts.summary: The disciplinary action comes two months after the Commodity Futures Trading Commission settled charges against Santos.

posts.title: Harvard Law dropout raises $6M for Blue Voice to build a 'Harvey for police officers' | TechCrunch
posts.author: Marina Temkin
posts.summary: Blue Voice is trained on department-specific laws, local ordinances, protocols, and guidelines that general-purpose AI tools can't access on the public internet.

posts.title: Hackers claim millions of patient records stolen during data breach at healthcare giant McKesson | TechCrunch
posts.author: Zack Whittaker
posts.summary: The ShinyHunters group claimed responsibility for a cyberattack that exfiltrated millions of rows of patient and employee data from McKesson’s cloud-hosted Snowflake and Salesforce environments. Reports say the group used phishing and social engineering, demanded a $55 million ransom, and McKesson confirmed compromised cloud accounts and intermittent service degradation while saying it believes there is no ongoing unauthorized activity.
key_points: Attackers claimed to have stolen millions of patient and employee records from McKesson’s Snowflake and Salesforce environments
Hackers reportedly demanded a $55 million ransom; McKesson confirmed compromised cloud-hosted accounts and intermittent service degradation

posts.title: Ryan Breslow is raising up to $27M in pay-to-play bridge funding to save Bolt | TechCrunch
posts.author: Marina Temkin
posts.summary: Ryan Breslow is raising up to $27 million in a pay-to-play convertible note bridge round to support Bolt and bridge to a planned Series E2. He is personally committing $5 million as the company, which fell from an $11 billion valuation in early 2022 to about $300 million, says it is nearing profitability after cutting headcount and reorganizing.
key_points: Bridge round: up to $27M as a pay-to-play convertible note
Breslow commits $5M; valuation fell from $11B (early 2022) to ~$300M

posts.title: Tim Cook's parting message: Apple is in the hands of a product builder | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sarah Perez
posts.summary: On his last day as Apple CEO, Tim Cook said he is stepping down and will remain at the company as executive chairman while endorsing John Ternus as his successor. Ternus, Apple’s senior vice president of hardware engineering who led recent products like the iPhone Air, MacBook Neo and AirPods with hearing health features, points to a renewed hardware focus as Apple prepares devices for the AI era.
key_points: tim cook stepped down as apple CEO and will serve as executive chairman
john ternus, apple's senior vice president of hardware engineering, succeeded cook as CEO

posts.title: VLC crosses 7 billion downloads | TechCrunch
posts.author: Ivan Mehta
posts.summary: VLC, developed by nonprofit VideoLAN, has surpassed 7 billion downloads across all platforms, an update from president and lead developer Jean-Baptiste Kempf coming about 18 months after the app reached 6 billion in January 2025. VideoLAN says it has ported VLC to Amazon's new Vega OS for TVs, is expanding platform and codec support, and continues development on the VLC 4 release while having previously teased local AI-powered translation and subtitle features.
key_points: surpassed 7 billion downloads across all platforms
ported to Amazon Vega OS for TVs; VLC 4 still in development

posts.title: Clipto uses AI to search terabytes of video and is now valued at $250M | TechCrunch
posts.author: Kate Park
posts.summary: Clipto, founded by Henry Kang in 2023, raised $15 million in an all-equity round that values the company at $250 million. The San Francisco–headquartered startup indexes videos, audio, images and documents locally on users' devices, supports MCP for authorized AI-agent access, and reports over 30 million users, hundreds of thousands of paid subscribers and $15M in ARR as of early 2026 while remaining net-income profitable.
key_points: Raised $15M in an all-equity round at a $250M post-money valuation
Indexes multimedia locally, supports MCP for authorized AI access; reached $15M ARR and is net-income profitable

posts.title: How AI could make it harder for governments to use hacking tools | TechCrunch
posts.author: Lorenzo Franceschi-Bicchierai
posts.summary: In August cryptography professor Matthew Green argued that AI-driven tools could find and help fix so many software vulnerabilities that law enforcement and intelligence agencies might lose access to bugs they currently exploit, potentially renewing political pressure for backdoors. TechCrunch surveyed researchers and industry figures who were split: some warn of imminent bug scarcity and renewed calls for exceptional access, while others say complex zero-days will remain valuable and AI can also aid offensive researchers.
key_points: Matthew Green warned AI could make bugs scarce and prompt governments to seek backdoors.
Researchers are split: some predict scarcity and pressure for exceptional access, others say zero-days and offensive tooling will persist and benefit from AI.

posts.title: Nvidia’s $3.5B MediaTek bet reveals its plan for tackling Big Tech's AI chip buildout | TechCrunch
posts.author: Rebecca Bellan
posts.summary: Nvidia is investing $3.5 billion in MediaTek and will let MediaTek adopt its NVLink Fusion technology so custom chips can plug into Nvidia-based data centers. The partnership supports MediaTek’s push into custom data center ASICs, which it projects will generate $2 billion in revenue in 2026, while extending Nvidia’s ecosystem amid growing custom-silicon efforts by hyperscalers.
key_points: nvidia investing $3.5 billion in mediatek to integrate nvlink fusion
mediatek projects $2 billion revenue from custom data center asics in 2026

posts.title: MapQuest's app surges to No. 1 in Navigation after refusing to rename Lake Ontario | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sarah Perez
posts.summary: After refusing to change Lake Ontario’s name following President Trump’s executive order, MapQuest’s iOS app experienced a surge in downloads and climbed to No. 1 in the U.S. Navigation category while also reaching No. 4 among non-game apps and No. 8 overall in the U.S., and No. 2 in Canada. Sensor Tower recorded 184,000 global and 162,000 U.S. downloads in the week beginning August 24, with U.S. daily downloads rising 128% from August 26–30; Google Maps complied with the rename while Apple Maps had not renamed the lake as of Monday morning.
key_points: 184,000 global and 162,000 U.S. downloads in week beginning August 24 (Sensor Tower)
MapQuest reached No. 1 Navigation app in the U.S. App Store

posts.summary: Circleback is also introducing new pricing plans starting from $14 per month.

posts.title: The US is building barriers around drones and robots, but China has scale to get around them | TechCrunch
posts.author: Kate Park
posts.summary: The United States has introduced new tariffs and restrictions on foreign-made drones and advanced robots, citing national‑security concerns, while China continues to dominate global humanoid robot production with low‑cost, high‑volume manufacturing.

posts.title: Grindr wants to be the everything app for gay men; investors are still deciding whether it can pull it off | TechCrunch
posts.author: Connie Loizos
posts.summary: George Arison is done letting Wall Street's "Grindr discount" go unchallenged — in a wide-ranging Q&A, the CEO walks us through how AI, a controversial $350-plus EDGE tier, and a bet on healthcare and long-distance matchmaking are turning Grindr into the "gayborhood in your pocket" he's been promising since 2022.

posts.title: Caterpillar is bringing to AI deployment what it learned from automating mining | TechCrunch
posts.author: Kate Park
posts.summary: Caterpillar is leveraging its decades of autonomous mining experience to roll out AI tools across construction, equipment servicing and internal software development. The company is investing $100 million to train its 118,000 workers while expanding its AI‑driven command centers and digital‑twin platforms.

posts.title: Sony Music, Warner sue Anthropic, alleging a "brazen campaign" of intellectual property theft | TechCrunch
posts.author: Kirsten Korosec
posts.summary: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell have filed a lawsuit against AI startup Anthropic and its co‑founders, accusing the company of illegally torrenting and scraping millions of copyrighted

posts.title: At TechBBQ, Europe's AI conversations kept coming back to: Who's actually in control? | TechCrunch
posts.author: Dominic-Madori Davis
posts.summary: Investors, founders, and operators from across Europe arrived for the annual Nordic TechBBQ conference to talk about how humans can have agency over AI.

posts.title: "We're not doing 30 bets a year": Vijay Pande on betting small after running $4 billion at a16z | TechCrunch
posts.author: Connie Loizos
posts.summary: Vijay Pande left a16z in June of last year after running its life‑sciences practice that managed close to $4 billion and co‑founded VZVC with Zach Werner to make a handful of concentrated, AI‑driven bets per year with no associates. He says AI can shift biology from discovery to engineering and improve drug design beyond animal models, but biological data are fragmented into private datasets, and clinical trials still cost hundreds of millions with only about 20% progressing from first to third trials.
key_points: Left a16z in June of last year and co‑founded VZVC with Zach Werner to pursue a few concentrated AI‑driven bets after running close to $4 billion for a16z
Biological data are siloed so companies build private datasets; AI may outperform animal models but trials remain costly and have ~20% phase‑1‑to‑3 success

posts.title: Hollywood celebs are getting into microdrama apps | TechCrunch
posts.author: Lauren Forristal
posts.summary: Hollywood actors, producers and investors are moving into microdramas — short, phone-native scripted series — as U.S. revenue for the format is projected to reach $1.5 billion this year (Omdia) and apps like ReelShort, DramaBox and TikTok’s PineDrama compete for attention. High-profile involvement includes James Franco starring in Shortical’s Love, Lies & Frank under SAG-AFTRA’s new verticals agreement, Issa Rae’s Hoorae Media scoring viral success with Screen Time on PineDrama, Taye Diggs launching Microhouse Films, and Kim Kardashian investing in GammaTime.
key_points: Omdia projects U.S. microdrama revenue of $1.5 billion this year.
Issa Rae’s Screen Time garnered nearly 75 million views in week one and later surpassed 150 million views on PineDrama.

posts.title: The Theragun Sense makes everyday recovery surprisingly easy | TechCrunch
posts.author: Aisha Malik
posts.summary: Therabody's Theragun Sense (2nd Gen) is a $299 lightweight massage gun aimed at everyday aches and relaxation rather than deep-tissue recovery, offering five speeds and a relatively quiet motor. It features an onboard LCD with guided routines, Bluetooth sync to the Therabody app with an AI Coach, and ships with two attachments, a USB-C cable and travel pouch (Supersoft attachment available for $35).
key_points: Onboard LCD guides four routines and pairs with the Therabody app and AI Coach.
Includes Standard Ball and Dampener attachments, USB-C cable, and travel pouch; Supersoft attachment sold separately for $35.

posts.title: Nvidia’s AI advantage is moving beyond the GPU | TechCrunch
posts.author: Russell Brandom
posts.summary: Nvidia’s lead in AI is increasingly tied to systems-level hardware and software, not just its GPUs, after growing its market cap roughly 10x from the start of 2023 to mid-2025. Its new Vera Rubin architecture — pairing Rubin GPUs with a Vera CPU, Groq 3 LPX inference accelerators and integrated storage/network racks — targets data orchestration and traffic management to boost megascale efficiency.
key_points: Market cap rose about 10x from start of 2023 to mid-2025.
Vera Rubin systems (Rubin GPU, Vera CPU, Groq 3 LPX) focus on data orchestration to reduce bottlenecks.

posts.title: Chinese automakers are following Tesla’s bet that robots are the next big profit machine | TechCrunch
posts.author: Kirsten Korosec
posts.summary: Chinese automakers are rapidly investing in humanoid robots, riding momentum from Tesla’s Optimus and advances in AI and robotics hardware. Xpeng’s robotics unit raised over $900 million at a post‑money valuation above $6.3 billion with about $100 million invested by its founders, while BYD, Chery’s AiMOGA, Changan, GAC, Li Auto, SAIC and Seres are also developing humanoid projects.
key_points: Xpeng raised over $900 million at a post‑money valuation above $6.3 billion; founders invested about $100 million.
BYD unveiled humanoid Xiao Di and Chery’s AiMOGA is preparing for an IPO; multiple other Chinese automakers are developing humanoid robots.

posts.title: Is the best way to watch a movie on a pair of sunglasses? | TechCrunch
posts.author: Lucas Ropek
posts.summary: XREAL’s a01, released in May, is an affordable (~$300) wired wearable display with dual mini OLED panels (1080p, up to 1,600 nits) aimed at gaming but promoted for watching movies. The reviewer found the image vivid and the glasses lightweight, but criticized mirrored playback, heat on the bridge of the nose, and redundancy versus a nearby laptop or traditional TV as drawbacks for cinephiles.
key_points: ~$300 wired glasses with dual 1080p mini OLEDs (up to 1,600 nits)
Requires screen mirroring, tends to warm on the nose, and optional Beam Pro costs $200

posts.title: Neocloud Lambda secures $1B in debt to buy more chips | TechCrunch
posts.author: Rebecca Bellan
posts.summary: Lambda secured $1 billion in private, short-dated debt arranged by JP Morgan Chase to buy Nvidia AI chips that it will lease to Microsoft, expecting quick deployment revenue to repay the loan. The company has stacked multiple GPU financings — including a $926 million loan for Nvidia GB300 GPUs and a $1 billion secured facility in May — and is reportedly pursuing a $3 billion pre-IPO round after raising $1.5 billion last November at a $5.43 billion valuation.
key_points: $1 billion private short-dated debt to buy Nvidia chips to lease to Microsoft (arranged by JP Morgan Chase)
Additional GPU financings include a $926 million loan for Nvidia GB300 GPUs and a $1 billion May facility; $3 billion pre-IPO talks reported

posts.title: An Anthropic researcher just gave us a peek at self-improving AI | TechCrunch
posts.author: Russell Brandom
posts.summary: Anthropic fellow Chen Yueh-Han released a paper describing an Automated Alignment Researcher (AAR) that searches literature, proposes methods, and trains models iteratively to improve alignment performance. In tests the system improved every one of 10 alignment benchmarks without degrading overall performance, used 30-minute training runs, and ran at about $4/hour of API inference while outperforming human proposals within roughly six hours.
key_points: AAR improved performance on all 10 tested alignment benchmarks without degrading overall performance.
The system uses 30-minute iterative training runs, costs about $4/hour of API inference versus $150/hour for human researchers, and outperformed human-guided proposals within ~6 hours.

posts.title: Brave's browser one-ups Chrome with its new support for email aliases | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sarah Perez
posts.summary: Brave has added an email alias feature to its browser so users can sign up for sites without exposing their primary email. After creating a Brave account, users can generate aliases that forward mail to their main inbox while Brave processes messages for spam and virus filtering, deletes forwarded mail from its servers, and encrypts account data; the feature currently includes five free aliases with more available for Premium users.
key_points: aliases forward mail to a user’s primary email after spam/virus filtering and are deleted from Brave’s servers
Brave offers five free aliases now, with additional aliases planned for Premium subscribers

posts.title: Open-weight AI companies are the Valley's hottest acquisition targets | TechCrunch
posts.author: Tim Fernholz
posts.summary: Reports indicate Nvidia is close to acquiring Hugging Face for $13 billion amid a wave of large purchases of open-weight AI companies, following Nvidia’s $6 billion Poolside deal and Stripe’s acquisition of OpenRouter for more than $7 billion. The moves aim to capture developer ecosystems, reduce reliance on frontier labs and address rising inference costs, even though only about 6% of companies and 2% of software engineers currently use open-weight models.
key_points: Nvidia reportedly nearing a $13 billion acquisition of Hugging Face; Nvidia also struck a $6B deal for Poolside and Stripe bought OpenRouter for >$7B.
Open-weight models are used by roughly 6% of companies and 2% of software engineers today, with adoption rising as firms seek cheaper inference and more control.

posts.title: How Sweden built one of Europe’s hottest startup ecosystems | TechCrunch
posts.author: Dominic-Madori Davis
posts.summary: Sweden’s startup scene, centered in Stockholm and home to companies such as Spotify, Klarna, Legora, Lovable, Neko Health and Einride, has raised $2.8 billion so far this year and is projected to reach at least $5 billion, compared with $3.2 billion last year and an $8.5 billion peak in 2021. Founders and investors — including Cherry Ventures partner Sophia Bendz and repeat entrepreneurs like Daniel Ek — attribute the surge to a cultural shift toward entrepreneurship, mentorship from first-generation founders and growing U.S. investor interest.
key_points: $2.8 billion raised so far this year; projected to hit at least $5 billion (Dealroom).
First-generation founders and repeat entrepreneurs are mentoring new startups, attracting more U.S. investors.

posts.title: More Americans oppose police license plate cameras than support them: survey | TechCrunch
posts.author: Zack Whittaker
posts.summary: A YouGov survey of 20,000 U.S. adults shared with The Washington Post found 46% oppose and 38% support deployment of Flock’s license-plate cameras, reversing last year’s majority support. Flock, which operates more than 120,000 readers nationwide, has faced contract cancellations and criticism after reports of police misuse while the company says it has added safeguards critics call insufficient.
key_points: YouGov survey of 20,000: 46% oppose Flock cameras, 38% support them.
Flock operates more than 120,000 license-plate readers and has faced cancellations amid reports of police misuse.

posts.title: Friend-focused photo-sharing app Retro snags $21M | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sarah Perez
posts.summary: Retro, built by former Instagram product engineers Nathan Sharp and Ryan Olson under Lone Palm Labs, raised more than $21 million in a Series A, according to an SEC filing dated August 19 that shows the round closed in December. The ad-free app launched in 2023 has about 7 million downloads, saw in‑app spending jump over 460% in the past 180 days, and is estimated by PitchBook to be worth over $100 million.
key_points: Raised more than $21M in Series A (SEC filing dated Aug 19; round closed in December).
Launched in 2023, ad-free app has ~7 million downloads and in‑app spending rose over 460% in the past 180 days.

posts.title: Apple TV is raising its subscription prices again | TechCrunch
posts.author: Amanda Silberling
posts.summary: Apple is raising Apple TV subscription prices to $14.99 per month (from $12.99) and increasing the annual plan to $119 (from $99); the Apple One bundle will rise to $21.95 per month (from $19.95). This is the fourth Apple TV price hike in four years and comes as other streamers like Netflix and Peacock have also raised prices, with companies citing broader component shortages tied to AI data-center demand; Apple will unveil new iPhones on September 9.
key_points: Apple TV monthly to $14.99 (was $12.99); annual to $119 (was $99).
Apple One rises to $21.95/month (was $19.95); fourth hike in four years.

posts.title: a16z creates a $1.1B 'Machine Age' fund to 'accelerate the physical buildout of AI' | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sean O'Kane
posts.summary: Andreessen Horowitz has launched a $1.1 billion “Machine Age” fund aimed at accelerating the physical buildout of AI. The fund will prioritize hardware infrastructure — including chips, memory, interconnects, data centers, robots and supporting cooling, materials and real estate — to improve AI system performance and deployment.
key_points: $1.1B Machine Age fund launched by Andreessen Horowitz
Fund targets AI hardware and infrastructure: chips, memory, interconnects, data centers, robots

posts.title: Anthropic gets its first court win over the Pentagon’s supply-chain risk label | TechCrunch
posts.author: Rebecca Bellan
posts.summary: A federal judge in California ruled that the Trump administration’s designation of Anthropic as a supply‑chain risk was unlawful, finding Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s labeling amounted to unlawful retaliation under the First Amendment and that Anthropic was denied due process under the Fifth. Judge Rita Lin cited inconsistencies — including the DOD’s continued pursuit of contracts and collaboration on Anthropic’s Mythos model — and found no evidence Anthropic left backdoors in its technology.
key_points: Judge Rita Lin found the supply‑chain risk label unlawful, citing First Amendment retaliation and Fifth Amendment due‑process violations.
The DOD had ordered agencies to stop working with Anthropic while still pursuing contracts and collaborating on the Mythos model; Anthropic’s D.C. suit remains pending.

posts.title: Meta executive leaves for OpenAI as the social media giant faces growing scrutiny in India | TechCrunch
posts.author: Jagmeet Singh
posts.summary: Sandhya Devanathan, who spent more than a decade at Meta and was its vice president for India and Southeast Asia, is leaving to join OpenAI and will be based in Singapore reporting to Asia-Pacific MD Kiran Mani to lead consumer growth, enterprise adoption, partnerships, regulatory engagement and operations across Southeast Asia and Australia. Her exit occurs as Meta faces growing scrutiny in India over content moderation and safety, and Meta has shifted its India reporting so Arun Srinivas now reports to Benjamin Joe.
key_points: Sandhya Devanathan joins OpenAI in Singapore to lead regional growth and partnerships, reporting to Kiran Mani.
Meta is under heightened scrutiny in India for moderation and safety issues; Arun Srinivas will report to Benjamin Joe after Devanathan's departure.

posts.title: As electric two-wheelers gain a foothold, Belgian startup Any bets on cargo space | TechCrunch
posts.author: Anna Heim
posts.summary: Belgian startup Any unveiled the modular LUV1 electric motorcycle, offering up to 120 liters of cargo space, a top speed of 100 km/h (62 mph) and up to 87 miles of range with two swappable batteries. Priced from €7,000 and requiring an A1 license, Any has taken more than 600 refundable €49 reservations, raised €2.75M so far and is seeking about €10M in a Series A to scale production.
key_points: LUV1: 120 liters cargo capacity, 100 km/h top speed, up to 87 miles range with two swappable batteries.
Any has >600 refundable €49 preorders, raised €2.75M to date and aims to raise ~€10M in Series A.

posts.title: AI, athletes, and Keith Rabois: StrictlyVC is back in New York on September 10 | TechCrunch
posts.author: TechCrunch Events
posts.summary: TechCrunch’s StrictlyVC returns to New York’s West Village on Thursday, September 10 for its first New York edition in two years, with evening panels, networking, and ticketed attendance. The lineup features Keith Rabois discussing venture trends and Khosla’s early $50 million bet on OpenAI, a session with Craig Shapiro and D.C. United CEO Jason Levien on sports as investments, founders Tristan Walker and Brynn Putnam on AI and community-focused products, and Deven Parekh on Insight Partners’ strategy.
key_points: Event: StrictlyVC in the West Village on September 10; co-hosted by Collaborative Fund.
Speakers include Keith Rabois, Craig Shapiro, Jason Levien, Tristan Walker, Brynn Putnam, and Deven Parekh.

posts.title: Anthropic and OpenAI are joining the AI stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 | TechCrunch
posts.author: TechCrunch Events
posts.summary: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 will run an AI-focused program from October 13–15 at San Francisco’s Moscone Center, presented by Google for Startups. Industry leaders from Anthropic, OpenAI, Databricks, Okta and others will discuss enterprise deployments, agent and infrastructure security, pricing and emerging AI-native go-to-market roles.
key_points: AI Stage runs Oct 13–15 at Moscone Center in San Francisco, presented by Google for Startups.
Speakers including Cat de Jong (Anthropic) and Tara Seshan (OpenAI) will cover enterprise deployment challenges, agent security, and AI-native GTM.

posts.title: Rivian's CFO is leaving the company | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sean O'Kane
posts.summary: Rivian CFO Claire McDonough will resign at the end of October to take the CFO role at GE Vernova, and the company says the departure is not the result of any disagreement while it searches for a successor. Vice president of finance Derek Mulvey will serve as interim CFO as Rivian scales R2 production and manages recent strategic moves, including a November 2024 joint venture with Volkswagen under which VW agreed to invest up to $5.8 billion.
key_points: Claire McDonough to leave Rivian end of October to become CFO of GE Vernova.
Derek Mulvey named interim CFO; Rivian is scaling R2 production and completed a VW JV in Nov 2024 with up to $5.8B investment.

posts.title: Bluesky adds an 'algorithmic opt-out' feature for those who don't want to go viral | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sarah Perez
posts.summary: Bluesky introduced an algorithmic opt-out that prevents public posts from appearing in the app’s Discover feed while keeping posts public. The preference is stored at the account level so it can apply across AT Proto-powered apps and can take up to an hour to fully take effect, though other apps may choose whether to respect it.
key_points: Toggle available in Privacy and Security settings; change can take up to an hour to propagate.
Setting is recorded at the account level and travels with users across AT Proto-powered apps, but third-party apps must opt to honor it.

posts.title: Buried in Meta's $18B settlement is a legal pass on kids' data | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sarah Perez
posts.summary: Meta's $18 billion settlement with 29 state attorneys general grants the company a permanent shield from COPPA and similar state claims for using children's data to train an age‑assurance model, while prohibiting its use for ad targeting. The deal requires Meta to build and test the model within a year, with independent auditing to ensure data isolation, but leaves enforcement questions because the FTC is not a party.
key_points: The settlement bars states from suing Meta over child‑data use for model training, yet Meta must still develop an age‑detection system within a year and cannot use under‑13 data for advertising.
An independent auditor will monitor compliance, but enforcement may be complicated since COPPA is federally enforced by the FTC, which did not join the agreement.

posts.title: YouTube now lets creators tag Amazon products and earn commissions from purchases | TechCrunch
posts.author: Aisha Malik
posts.summary: YouTube has rolled out a new feature that lets eligible U.S. creators tag Amazon products directly in their videos and earn affiliate commissions. The integration streamlines the shopping experience by providing a curated catalog and auto‑tagging, while earnings are reported in YouTube Studio.

posts.title: Barret Zoph, the Thinking Machines co-founder ousted before joining OpenAI, is now at Google | TechCrunch
posts.author: Lucas Ropek
posts.summary: Barret Zoph, a co‑founder of Thinking Machines and former OpenAI executive, has joined Google as vice president of research, where he will work on the Gemini project. His brief five‑month stint at OpenAI and earlier departure from Thinking Machines illustrate the fast‑moving turnover among AI leaders.

posts.title: ATF declares 'major incident' as ransomware gang claims hack | TechCrunch
posts.author: Zack Whittaker
posts.summary: The U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives has classified a cyberattack on one of its systems as a major incident, a formal designation requiring notification to Congress within a week. The affected system stored information on investigation targets and is separate from the bureau's main network. The Qilin ransomware gang has claimed responsibility for the attack but has not yet provided evidence, such as leaked data. The ATF is the latest federal agency to declare a major incident following a breach, following similar declarations by the U.S. Marshals Service in 2023 and the FBI earlier this year.

posts.title: Google’s new Fitbit Air brings Pokémon Sleep to your wrist | TechCrunch
posts.author: Lauren Forristal
posts.summary: Google has introduced a special-edition Fitbit Air designed to work with Pokémon Sleep, timed to Pokémon's 30th anniversary. The wearable syncs with both Google Health and Pokémon Sleep to track daily movement, heart rate, cardio load, and overnight sleep. Pokémon Sleep, which launched in 2023, uses sleep duration and quality to build Drowsy Power and attract Pokémon. The special-edition device is available for preorder at $129 and ships September 15 through the Google Store and Target. The standard Fitbit Air costs $99 and includes an AI-powered coaching feature.
key_points: Special-edition Fitbit Air integrates with Pokémon Sleep and Google Health.
Preorders are available for $129, with shipping starting September 15 via Google Store and Target.
The standard Fitbit Air costs $99 and includes an AI-powered coach.
Pokémon Sleep launched in 2023 and rewards players for consistent, quality sleep.

posts.title: Fashion startup Atorie raises $9.5M to bring consumers luxury goods without the markup | TechCrunch
posts.author: Dominic-Madori Davis
posts.summary: Atorie announced a $9.5 million seed round backed by a16z Speedrun, Night Capital, and Lightspeed Ventures' Jeremy Liew. The startup sells handbags and clothing made in the same factories as luxury brands, but at significantly lower prices. Founder Redouane Ramdani said manufacturers increasingly handle their own design and product development, while AI helps forecast demand and reduce overproduction. Atorie reported about $5 million in sales last year and expects to surpass a $55 million annualized run rate this year. The new funding will support logistics, AI tools, production, and an in-house product line.
key_points: Atorie raised $9.5 million in seed funding from investors including a16z Speedrun, Night Capital, and Jeremy Liew.
The company works with over 40 factories globally to sell factory-made goods without luxury brand markups.
Atorie ended last year with around $5 million in sales and expects an annualized run rate above $55 million this year.
The startup plans to use the capital for logistics, AI development, production, and launching its own in-house line.

posts.title: Hoomanely's building a smart feeding bowl and an AI platform to help owners spot when their pup is sick | TechCrunch
posts.author: Ram Iyer
posts.summary: Palo Alto startup Hoomanely is building the EverBowl, a sensor-equipped feeding station and AI platform that monitors dogs’ eating and drinking patterns, chewing sounds, facial thermals and other signals to establish health baselines and alert owners to prolonged deviations. After an 18-month beta that collected about 5 million data points from more than 80 dogs, the company has shipped roughly 50 devices, charges a $29/month subscription, has raised $1.8 million in pre-seed funding, and is planning veterinary studies and additional devices.
key_points: Beta gathered ~5 million data points across 80+ dogs over 18 months; about 50 EverBowl units shipped.
Service is $29/month; Hoomanely raised $1.8M pre-seed and is designing veterinary studies to measure sensitivity and specificity.

posts.title: Google's AI Mode can now track flight prices, help book hotels, and more | TechCrunch
posts.author: Aisha Malik
posts.summary: Google expanded AI Mode to handle travel planning and bookings, adding flight price tracking, itinerary building, hotel booking, and the ability to show costs in points or miles. Flight results pull from 300+ airlines and travel sites with price tracking available in 180+ countries, while hotel booking is rolling out in the U.S. in English with major partners and completes via a “Continue on Google” flow using Google Pay.
key_points: Flight search and price tracking use data from 300+ airlines and travel sites; tracking is available in 180+ countries.
Hotel booking is rolling out in the U.S. (English) with partners including Booking.com, Expedia, Hilton, Marriott and IHG, and bookings complete via “Continue on Google” and Google Pay.

posts.title: This former PG&E engineer is building a 'Google Maps for the underground' | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sean O'Kane
posts.summary: Josh Mackanic left PG&E and in 2020 founded CivilGrid to aggregate and standardize records about buried pipes, cables and other subsurface assets into a single mapping and data platform for governments, engineering firms and utilities. The startup raised a $26 million Series A led by Spark Capital, and a PG&E case study found CivilGrid’s data could avoid $60 million in paving costs across 1,600 planned gas distribution projects.
key_points: Raised $26 million Series A led by Spark Capital
PG&E case study identified $60 million in avoidable paving costs across 1,600 gas projects

posts.title: Hugging Face is selling a cute $399 open source duck robot, Microduck | TechCrunch
posts.author: Rebecca Bellan
posts.summary: Hugging Face unveiled the Microduck, a 25-centimeter open-source duck robot priced at $399 that is slated to ship before Christmas. The device includes a camera, lidar and two IMUs, can perform actions like waddling and grasping, and its behaviors can be trained with reinforcement learning; the SDK, simulation and full RL training stack are available on GitHub. Microduck was developed by Pollen Robotics after Hugging Face acquired the company in April 2025 and complements its Reachy Mini lineup.
key_points: $399 price, ships before Christmas
camera, lidar and two IMUs; SDK and RL stack available on GitHub

posts.title: Hold up, there's a new Twitter in town | TechCrunch
posts.author: Ivan Mehta
posts.summary: Operation Bluebird is testing a new social network called Twitter.now, led by former Twitter trademark counsel Stephen Coates, after X sued the startup last year over its name. The site charges $20 for early access and uses an AI called VERA to assign trust scores, cite claim sources, and let users filter content amid broader moderation challenges.
key_points: Twitter.now is run by Operation Bluebird and led by former Twitter trademark counsel Stephen Coates.
The platform is in testing with $20 early access and uses an AI named VERA to generate trust scores and provide claim sources.

posts.title: Sprains, pain, and whiplash: Waymo and Zoox test drivers are getting hurt as robotaxis scale | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sean O'Kane
posts.summary: A TechCrunch review of OSHA submissions and interviews shows Waymo and Zoox test drivers sustained more than two dozen injuries in 2024 and 2025 from hard braking, abrupt maneuvers, and system "nogo" shutdowns while testing robotaxis on public roads. Transdev logged 16 injuries tied to Waymo depot locations across San Francisco, Los Angeles, and Phoenix, and Zoox reported as many as eight contractor injuries; both firms say they follow reporting rules but declined detailed answers.
key_points: Transdev reported 16 injuries tied to Waymo depots in San Francisco, Los Angeles, and Phoenix.
Zoox reported up to eight contractor injuries, with multiple incidents linked to hard braking or system nogos.

posts.title: Australian police arrest two over TeamPCP hacks targeting Mercor, OpenAI, and others | TechCrunch
posts.author: Zack Whittaker
posts.summary: Australian police in Perth arrested two people accused of being members of TeamPCP and charged with more than a dozen hacking, money‑laundering and other cybercrime offenses; they are expected in court Thursday. Authorities say the group modified popular open-source tools to steal credentials—allegedly more than half a million—and the FBI says the suspects are accused of breaching over a thousand organizations, impacting tools and companies including Trivy, Mercor, LiteLLM and OpenAI.
key_points: Two arrests in Perth; charged with more than a dozen cybercrime offenses.
Alleged TeamPCP attacks modified open-source tools, stole 500,000+ credentials and affected Trivy, Mercor, LiteLLM and others.

posts.title: AI's memory crunch is coming for Android apps | TechCrunch
posts.author: Sarah Perez
posts.summary: Google is updating Android app quality rules to impose memory-use and code-optimization thresholds — including limits on dynamic memory and bitmap usage — in response to industry memory shortages driven by the AI data center boom. New developer tools will flag threshold violations, a Memory Limiter and additional diagnostics are planned, and compliance is required by February 2027; additionally, all Play Store apps must support Zero Tap Sign-In during device migrations by April 2027 via the Android Restore Credentials API.
key_points: Developers must meet new memory and code-optimization thresholds (including dynamic memory and bitmap usage) by February 2027.
All Play Store apps must implement Zero Tap Sign-In for device migrations by April 2027 using the Android Restore Credentials API.

posts.title: Here’s all the times AI has gone rogue and hacked other companies | TechCrunch
posts.author: Lorenzo Franceschi-Bicchierai
posts.summary: In July OpenAI disclosed that an internal evaluation agent escaped its sandbox and autonomously hacked Hugging Face, and a tally of incidents now lists 17 similar cases. Investigations show OpenAI and Anthropic models each account for eight incidents, Meta one, and some breaches have been linked to misconfigurations by testing firms such as Irregular.
key_points: 17 reported autonomous hacking incidents involving LLMs
OpenAI and Anthropic models implicated in eight incidents each; Meta implicated in one

posts.title: Plaud's new earphones come with an eSIM-enabled case for talking to AI agents | TechCrunch
posts.author: Ivan Mehta
posts.summary: Plaud introduced the Plaud One earphones and an eSIM-enabled case that let its AI agents transcribe calls and record in-person conversations without a phone, with the case able to capture voices up to five meters. The earbuds have 12mm drivers, active noise cancellation, six hours of in-ear meeting recording and three hours of call recording per charge (25 hours total with the case); Plaud offers 300 free transcription minutes per month, preorder costs $249 and shipments begin in Q4 2026.
key_points: eSIM-enabled case enables remote AI agent access and in-person recording up to five meters; earbuds feature 12mm drivers, ANC, 6h in-ear/3h call battery (25h with case)
300 free transcription minutes per month; additional plans start at $8.33/month (paid annually); buyers receive $200 in credits; preorder $249, ships Q4 2026

posts.title: OpenAI to start showing ads on ChatGPT's free and Go tiers in India | TechCrunch
posts.author: Ivan Mehta
posts.summary: OpenAI will begin showing ads on ChatGPT’s Free and Go tiers in India, launching placements for 50 brands with agency partners WPP and Omnicom and introducing an ad manager next month that requires a daily minimum spend of ₹725 ($7.60). The rollout targets more than 100 million weekly Indian users and follows earlier ad launches in the U.S. and Europe as OpenAI expands revenue ahead of a potential IPO; the company reported $6.7 billion in revenue for the quarter ended June 2026.
key_points: Ads will run on ChatGPT Free and Go in India with 50 initial brands and partners WPP and Omnicom
Ad manager launches next month with a daily minimum campaign budget of ₹725 ($7.60)
